So I made some big improvements so that parsing for v1 and v2 is more successful, but 2 things came out of my reviewing/testing the code:

1. Wireshark has mechanisms to support the "non-packet meta data".  I _think_ that may be how the different message types should be handled, but I was not going to worry about adding that support in this patch.  My "real world" exposure to PEAK didn't have traces with these events (because the CAN bus was usually happy), but I understand wanting to be complete in supporting the file format (and help debug when there are issues on the bus).
2. A few years ago I wrote a text2pcap derived application to convert .trc files into pcap files.  This patch is the much better way to go (and the reason I am very interested in the functionality).  However, I'm not sure the SocketCAN format is what we should be shooting for.  The SocketCAN format seems to have a lot of padding that the current functionality is "forcing in" and the dissection just doesn't look that clean.  My converter was able to use the Linux SLL CAN types of the PCAP file format and to me, it looks cleaner when loading into Wireshark.  So that's what I want this patch to shoot for, but at the moment, I don't know how to do that.

Attached are the capture files used for testing (from links Miklós provided) that do provide ways to exercise the full file format.

[peak_trc_samples.zip](/uploads/5fe4b96c43fdca06cec6c057b85eea08/peak_trc_samples.zip)

> However, I'm not sure the SocketCAN format is what we should be shooting for. The SocketCAN format seems to have a lot of padding that the current functionality is "forcing in" and the dissection just doesn't look that clean.

I have picked SocketCAN just arbitrarily, or more exactly because Busmaster used the same. 

I am very glad that you are working on this, in the meantime I was also started to work on importer for Vector ASC files, that will also get benefit from your improvements if I find some time to finish it.
Please add me as a reviewer when you submit the Vector ASC MR.  I haven't worked with these file types, but am generally familiar with CAN packet behavior.

For sure! If we got into the ASC topic: ASC files could contain dumps from several interfaces at the same time. Do you have recommendation how to handle this? Ideally I would need to show a message dialog with a dropdown with 1-255 interface numbers (or filtered by the numbers present in the file). Do you happen to know any example of similar behavior? 

Btw. PEAK traces also coutaining busnumber, although I have not seen logs capturing more than one bus. 

Tomorrow I can play with multiple CAN adapters to see if PCANView is capable to record multiple interfaces.

I will review and test this MR with some more logs I have.

I did add support in PEAK for the busnumber being the packet interface ID, but there is some UAT preferences within the socketCAN dissector to allow it to be filterable that I didn't quite understand (looks like there's a bug, but it's probably a misunderstanding on my part)

(Re)reading the PEAK CAN TRC file documentation as well as LINKTYPE_CAN_SOCKETCAN section at tcpdump.org, I think there is still a little bit of "round peg, square hole" trying to conform to the SocketCAN metadata for "errors and events" that are in the TRC file. But for "regular packet data", I think it works well. I made some changes regarding "error packets" because the PEAK wiretap was providing (non-zero) data that the socketcan dissector was ignoring because PEAK had the "flag data" incorrect.  This is the "round peg, square hole" example where I think providing 0s for data is better and PEAK "error information" must be ignored.

At this point, I think this MR is good to go, and a separate MR can be created for non-packet event data.
